title: Control Tower and the landing zone: an account that starts out right

videos.script: Lessons 3 and 4 built a tree of accounts and hung rules on it, one command at a time. {{tree}} That works once. It does not work for the account somebody creates next March, in a hurry. {{next}} A landing zone is the answer: the whole arrangement, set up so that every new account starts out right. Logs, rules and a way in for people are all in place before anybody runs anything. {{lz}} AWS sells one, called Control Tower. It builds a security branch with two accounts, one for logs and one for audit. It turns on a trail and a recorder in every account. {{ct}} Its rules come in three kinds. Some refuse a request. Some report a resource after it exists. And some check a template before it builds anything. {{controls}} Your lab has no Control Tower, and this lesson says so plainly. So you will build the same shape by hand, with one script, and then look hard at what the script leaves out. {{script}} You will also put a price on what a landing zone switches on, from the price list. Free to set up is not the same as free to run. {{end}}
